newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan commercialises state telecom body.
newsitem.headline: Jordan commercialises state telecom body.

text.p: Jordan's profitable state telecommunications monopoly has been transformed into a public shareholding company as a first step towards its privatisation, officials said on Wednesday.

Officials said the wholly state-owned Telecommunications Corporation (TCC) was officially registered as a publicly listed company, whose shares would still be held by the government, as a first step towards privatisation.
The new Jordan Telecommunications Company, with 250 million dinars ($353 million) capital, will be the largest capitalised company to be registered in Jordan, officials said.
The company is also seeking financial advisers to help divest a 26 percent stake to a strategic partner.
It seeks applications by October 15 from world class firms or consortia with experience in similar state divestitures.
TCC revenues exceeded 123 million dinars ($173 million) in the first seven months of the year with a target of 180 million dinars for 1996, officials said.
A law passed last year set up a regulatory body to oversee the telecommunications sector, with powers to regulate pricing and licensing of private companies operating in the sector.

Industry officials say the telecoms business in Jordan offers huge potential in a country with 350,000 telephone numbers in a population of over four million. The government began awarding tenders since 1994 in a project to add an extra 440,000 telephone lines by 1998.
Jordan last month offered the sale of a 20 percent stake in Jordan Cement Factories to a strategic partner.
The offer was Jordan's first tangible step towards selling a profitable majority state-owned concern under a privatisation plan seen as key to the success of its IMF-guided economic reforms.
